● Audit complete. Here's the verdict.

  cart/editor external-cart dependency audit

  104 files scanned. The editor is almost entirely self-contained. Exactly one file reaches into another cart, and it's
  the one you'd expect.

  The only escape: cart/editor/stage/WorldEditorSurface.tsx → cart/hmsc-int

  line 3:  import { LoaderIsoView }      from '../../hmsc-int/LoaderIsoView'      ← VALUE import (real blocker)
  line 4:  import type { PlacedBuildPiece } from '../../hmsc-int/game/build/placed' ← type-only
  line 5:  import type { Armed }         from '../../hmsc-int/buildArmed'          ← type-only
  line 6:  import type { BuildEditEvent } from '../../hmsc-int/game'               ← type-only

  Only one of the four is a runtime value import (LoaderIsoView, mounted as the world-editor's iso viewer). The other
  three are import type — erased at bundle time, but they're still source-level couplings that will fail
  typecheck/resolution the moment hmsc-int is gone.

  Everything else is clean

  I enumerated every import specifier in the tree. Beyond that one file, the editor only pulls from:
  - itself — ./x and ../{data,design,dialogs,inspector,library,model,render3d,shell,stage,textures,world,...} (verified
  every root resolves inside cart/editor)
  - framework runtime/ — ../../../runtime/* (not a cart — the framework layer)
  - doors — @reactjit/*
  - react

  One red herring, cleared

  cart/editor/data/hmscAssetCatalog.ts looks like an hmsc dependency by name, but it lives inside the editor and is
  self-contained — its only imports are framework runtime/hooks/fs plus editor-internal modules. Same for
  content.ts/catalog.ts importing it locally. Not an escape.

  Bottom line

  Dropping the hmsc-int cart breaks exactly one file (WorldEditorSurface.tsx). To make the editor fully free-standing
  you'd need to either (a) port LoaderIsoView + the placed/buildArmed/game types into cart/editor, or (b) accept that
  WorldEditorSurface is the seam and cut/stub it. No other file in the cart cares that hmsc-int exists.

  I left req_2437 in doing (not flipping to review per your standing preference on audits). Want me to go ahead and
  sever that seam — port LoaderIsoView and those types into the editor so hmsc-int can safely die?

  WorldEditorSurface.tsx — the editor's "world" tab, in its current minimal form

  It's a ~50-line React wrapper that mounts the world-building surface inside the new editor. That's the whole file.
  What it actually does:

  - Holds a list of placed pieces (pieces) and one "armed" piece (currently hardcoded to floor.concrete.common — "no
  palette yet") in React state.
  - Mounts LoaderIsoView (borrowed from hmsc-int) as the actual iso 3D authoring surface.
  - On each click-to-place, LoaderIsoView's existing resolveAt→placeAt→set_live_pieces path drops a floor tile and
  renders it live, no rebake. onCommit just appends the placement to the React list.

  The header comment says it straight: this was the minimal "put something on the map" step (req_2401). It deliberately
  runs the fast/laundered path — JS holds the piece list, the TS GAME_BUILD.placed does the placement math — and
  explicitly flags that the "un-laundered" version is the next step: the framework owns the piece list, build.zig does 
  placement, the host renders + picks — and it names req_2349 as "the ported brain."

● Yeah — you've got it exactly, and it's not a phantom I invented. It's the real thing:

  When you open a document whose kind === 'world' (the map-making surface), the editor's Stage renders 
  WorldEditorSurface — cart/editor/stage/Stage.tsx:67:

  {activeDocument.kind === 'world' ? (
    <WorldEditorSurface />

  So the chain is: you click the world tab (the world-icon tab in StageTabs.tsx — HW_StageWorldTab) → that activates a
  world-kind document → the Stage swaps in WorldEditorSurface → which mounts LoaderIsoView, the iso map-making editor.

  So "world tab" = the tab with the world icon that loads the map-making editor. Same thing you're describing.
  WorldEditorSurface.tsx is just the thin React shell sitting between "that tab is active" and "the iso map editor

  That's the whole reason this one file is the single seam: the map-making editor surface itself (LoaderIsoView) still 
  physically lives in the hmsc-int cart, and WorldEditorSurface reaches across to borrow it.

  port the build catalog (36 rows + lookup) to Zig
  port build edit/contract/tag composition to Zig
  port build leaf geometry (bounds/roofRise/wall-lift) to Zig
  port placementFor / validatePlacement to Zig

  So what's actually still tethering the editor to hmsc-int

  Not the native loader (it's host doors — available from anywhere). Not the build brain (now in Zig). It's purely that
  the 1,206-line React glue component LoaderIsoView.tsx still physically sits in cart/hmsc-int/, and WorldEditorSurface
  reaches across the cart boundary to mount it.

  Cutting the seam therefore means one of two things — and this is the decision that's yours:

  1. Move LoaderIsoView.tsx (+ its small support files like buildArmed, the placed types) into cart/editor/ — mechanical
  relocation, and it keeps working since the heavy lifting is already host doors + the Zig brain.
  2. Rewrite the glue thinner now that the brain is in Zig — the JS placement/catalog paths it still calls could route
  to the ported framework/game/build.zig host doors instead, shrinking that 1,206-line file substantially.

  hmsc-int, or is it already calling the ported Zig host path? That tells us whether the port is wired-in or just
  sitting there compiled-but-unused. Want me to check that, or is that enough of the map for now?

  - The 2D painter's behavior (it was fucked — the behavior dies)

  2. UV character mesh editor — ported last, to Zig, TS dies with it.

  And the through-line: bones/skeleton replaces all of it. bones_loader.zig means you author a skeleton of a thing + how

  - And since wall/floor placement already works, the move isn't "preserve 583 files." It's: bring the live iso-world 
  path into cart/editor, slimmed to exactly what placement touches, and let the dead tail (skinBrush, cookedAssets, 
  compile/worldGeometry, the prop pieceMeshes) fall off. Those big imports are the science project, not the wall/floor
  path.

  The one discipline I'll hold: verify what the live wall/floor path actually calls before I cut, so I don't sever the
  working thing while trimming the fat around it.

  So my plan is: trace the live placement path through LoaderIsoView, pull that path into cart/editor as a slimmed local

  per you).
